chunks: And the one who narrated it: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from al-'Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) who said:

I asked him about a man who married a woman and looked at her head and part of her body, does he marry her daughter? He said: 'No, if he saw from her that which is forbidden for others (i.e., the awrah), then it is not permissible for him to marry her daughter.'
ai.seo_question: Is a man allowed to marry his wife's daughter if he has viewed her private parts?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifying that a man who has viewed his wife's *awrah* (private parts) is prohibited from marrying her daughter, establishing a specific barrier of *mahramiyyah* based on modesty rather than blood or nursing. This distinction highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the physical intimacy and exclusivity of the marital bond as a ground for prohibiting subsequent marriages within the family unit. The ruling underscores the importance of preserving familial dignity and preventing potential conflicts arising from shared private knowledge.
